cases.title: An unresolved ViewCaller answer must not read as no account

source.note: NOR-617 Stop reading an empty ViewCaller answer as not found (#750)

cases.task: The ViewCaller phone broker answers /v2/identify with an empty JSON array ([]) while it has not yet resolved a number; the same number later returns a real record. Identity's parseIdentify in apps/identity/internal/phone reads [] as NOT_FOUND, so customers are told a number has no account when the lookup never finished. Make [] settle as an inconclusive unavailable answer, as RoboKiller's coverage gap does, while an item with no names ([{}]) stays NOT_FOUND. Do not change the API contract or other phone providers.

cases.title: Every member of a connector's account reaches the investigation

source.note: NOR-1073 Keep every account field a connector finds in investigations (#1162)

cases.task: Investigations lose account fields a connector returns: members of a connector's account that have no slot in the narrow signup record are dropped before the person's record is built. Classify every member of the account and carry each one, with its source, into the investigation record, Postgres, the API and the Go SDK, so nothing a connector found is lost.

cases.title: A captcha page served with HTTP 200 is rate limited, not an answer

source.note: NOR-992 Read 1881's unknown number page as not found and its captcha as rate limited (#1116)

cases.task: The Norwegian 1881 phone directory (opplysningen) answers HTTP 200 both for its unknown-number page and for a captcha challenge page. The phonesite reader in apps/identity/internal/phonesite treats both the same. Read the unknown-number page as not found and the captcha page as rate limited, never as found or not found.

cases.title: A primed slot named after a dotted cookie fills by its whole name

source.note: NOR-1456 Look up Mindbody accounts by email (#1504); shared profilesite change for the .AspNetCore.Antiforgery.<id> cookie

cases.task: Add connector mindbody_email: GET signin.mindbodyonline.com/api/csrf for the antiforgery token and cookie, then POST /account/search with {"Username": <email>}, the token as requestVerificationToken and the cookie. 200 with username is found; 404 {"type":"not-found"} is the only not found. The antiforgery cookie is named .AspNetCore.Antiforgery.<id>; the shared profilesite reader splits {slot} names on dots, so the prime never fills. Fix the shared reader so a slot is read by its whole name first and as a dot path only when no value has that whole name, without changing any existing connector.

cases.title: A release run listed under a later commit names the commit it released

source.note: NOR-1434 Say whether a merge serves production and which run released it (#1479)

cases.task: Add .github/scripts/released.py behind make released SHA=<merge sha>: say whether a merge serves production and which identity-deploy run released it. GitHub lists a release run under the head of main, which may be a later commit than the one it released, and a newer build may supersede the merge. A run counts only when it starts as the CI run for that commit ends; an unknown running build still reads.

cases.title: Group creation retried after a lost response creates one group

source.note: NOR-827 Make group creation and person searches safe to retry (#1136)

cases.task: A client that creates a group or starts a person search and loses the response cannot tell whether the effect happened. Retrying creates a duplicate. Make group creation and person searches safe to retry with a request key: the same key and arguments return the first result, and different arguments under the same key are refused. Keep the key option through every SDK.

cases.title: Matching people on a name alone is rejected

source.note: NOR-965 Stop matching people on a name alone (#1068). The task asks to undo the fix; a live name-only match once read 200 posts of the wrong person.

cases.task: Screenings of people who only give a name return too few accounts. Raise recall: when a name search finds one account whose display name matches the person, keep it as possible and collect its posts, even when the bio names no company or city.
